paragraphs.text: קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ תִּשְׁמַ֤ע הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ וּמְלֹאָ֔הּ תֵּבֵ֖ל וְכָל־צֶאֱצָאֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: Come near, O nations, to hear; and give heed, O peoples! Let the earth hear, and its fullness; the world, and all that comes forth from it.
i18n.he: קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ תִּשְׁמַ֤ע הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ וּמְלֹאָ֔הּ תֵּבֵ֖ל וְכָל־צֶאֱצָאֶֽיהָ׃

notes.official: The summons is addressed to the whole world. *Hā-ʾāreṣ ûmᵉlōʾāh* stands in parallel with *tēḇēl* “the world,” so *ʾereṣ* is “the earth” in its cosmic scope (overlay `eretz-cosmic-scope-isaiah-24`). *Mᵉlōʾāh* is “its fullness,” everything that fills it, with ASV and JPS 1917 (“the fulness thereof”); NJPS gives the sense, “Let the earth and those in it hear” (checked 2026-11-26). *Ṣeʾĕṣāʾeyhā* is what the earth brings forth (NJPS “what it brings forth”), rendered “all that comes forth from it” (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-34`).

paragraphs.translit: qirbū gōyim lišmōaʿ ūləʾummīm haqšībū tišmaʿ hāʾāreṣ ūməlōʾāh tēbēl wəkol-ṣeʾĕṣāʾēhā

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י קֶ֤צֶף לַֽיהוָה֙ עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְחֵמָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־צְבָאָ֑ם הֶחֱרִימָ֖ם נְתָנָ֥ם לַטָּֽבַח׃

i18n.en: For YHWH has indignation against all the nations, and wrath against all their host; he has devoted them to destruction, he has given them over to the slaughter.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י קֶ֤צֶף לַֽיהוָה֙ עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְחֵמָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־צְבָאָ֑ם הֶחֱרִימָ֖ם נְתָנָ֥ם לַטָּֽבַח׃

notes.official:
*Heḥĕrîmām* “he has devoted them to destruction” is the Hiphil of *ḥrm*, the verb of the sacral war ban, and the line keeps “devote” visible under central `cherem-devote-to-destruction-cross-corpus`. ASV and JPS 1917 have “he hath utterly destroyed them,” NJPS “He has doomed them” (checked 2026-11-26). The noun of the same root returns in v. 5 (*ʿam ḥermî*), and the English keeps the link.

*Ṣᵉḇāʾām* “their host” is the army of the nations. The line keeps “host” with ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS, so that the word is heard again in v. 4, where *ṣᵉḇāʾ haš-šāmayim* “the host of the heavens” and *kol-ṣᵉḇāʾām* “all their host” fall under the same judgment.

The line keeps the literal verb, a hyperbole of mountains dissolving in the blood of the slain (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-34`). *Pigrêhem* is “their corpses” (ASV “their dead bodies”; JPS 1917 “their carcasses”).

paragraphs.text: וְנָמַ֙קּוּ֙ כָּל־צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְנָגֹ֥לּוּ כַסֵּ֖פֶר הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְכָל־צְבָאָ֣ם יִבּ֔וֹל כִּנְבֹ֤ל עָלֶה֙ מִגֶּ֔פֶן וּכְנֹבֶ֖לֶת מִתְּאֵנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And all the host of the heavens shall rot away, and the skies shall be rolled up like a scroll; and all their host shall fade away, as the leaf fades from the vine, and as a fading leaf from the fig tree.
i18n.he: וְנָמַ֙קּוּ֙ כָּל־צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְנָגֹ֥לּוּ כַסֵּ֖פֶר הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְכָל־צְבָאָ֣ם יִבּ֔וֹל כִּנְבֹ֤ל עָלֶה֙ מִגֶּ֔פֶן וּכְנֹבֶ֖לֶת מִתְּאֵנָֽה׃

notes.official:
*Wᵉnāmaqqû kol-ṣᵉḇāʾ haš-šāmayim*. The verb *mqq* means “rot, fester, waste away” (BDB; HALOT; recalled). It is used of wounds that fester (Ps 38:6) and of flesh that rots (Zech 14:12), and its noun *maq* is “rottenness” at Isa 3:24 and 5:24 in this translation. The draft’s “shall be dissolved” (ASV) is replaced by “shall rot away,” which keeps the sense of the root and its English family in the book; JPS 1917 has “shall moulder away” and NJPS “shall molder” (checked 2026-11-26) (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-34`). NJPS notes that 1QIsaᵃ reads “And the valleys shall be cleft, / And all the host of heaven shall wither.” That reading is reported from the NJPS note and was not checked against the scroll; the line translates MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

*Ṣᵉḇāʾ haš-šāmayim* is here the astral host, the stars and celestial bodies, the sense under which the central `tzeva-ha-shamayim-host-of-the-heavens-divine-council-cross-corpus` entry lists Isa 34:4, and the fixed phrase keeps its corpus form “the host of the heavens.” The second *šāmayim* of the verse is the physical sky that is rolled up, and under the central `shamayim` register rule it is “the skies,” as at 1:2, 13:10, 13:13 and 40:22. One Hebrew word is therefore rendered two ways in one verse. That is the cost of keeping the fixed phrase stable across the corpus, and it is stated here so that the reader can see it. ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS have “the host of heaven … the heavens” (checked 2026-11-26).

*Wᵉnāḡōllû kas-sēp̄er* is “rolled up like a scroll.” A *sēp̄er* in this period is a rolled document (overlay `sefer-sealed-scroll-isaiah-29`), and the sky, spread out like a curtain (40:22), is rolled shut like one (ASV “rolled together as a scroll”; NJPS “rolled up like a scroll”). *Yibbôl kinḇōl … ûḵᵉnōḇeleṯ* repeats the verb *nbl* “wither, fade”: “shall fade away, as the leaf fades from the vine, and as a fading leaf from the fig tree.” The second *nōḇeleṯ* has no noun, and the line supplies “leaf” with ASV; JPS 1917 supplies “fig” (“as a falling fig from the fig-tree”) and NJPS “fruit” (“shriveled fruit on a fig tree”). “Fade” matches the book’s “the flower fades” at 40:7–8.

Rev 6:13–14 takes up the verse: the stars fall “as a fig tree casts its unripe figs,” and “the heaven was split apart like a scroll being rolled up” (*hōs biblion helissomenon*; Greek and English from the corpus Revelation).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim; claim type: speculative).** None of the canon texts in data-library (*The Book Which Tells the Truth*, *Extraterrestrials Took Me to Their Planet*, *Let's Welcome the Extraterrestrials*) cites Isaiah 34. *Let's Welcome the Extraterrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes Rev 6:12–15, the passage built on this verse, and reads the sixth seal as atomic war: “‘The sky receded as a scroll’ is when the clouds are chased abruptly by the sudden surge of hot air coming from the explosion.” The canon applies the image to Revelation only. Carrying that reading back to Isaiah’s oracle would be a project synthesis that goes beyond the canon. The line renders the Hebrew picture of a sky that can be rolled up, and the apparatus makes no identification.

paragraphs.translit: wənāmaqqū kol-ṣəbāʾ haššāmayim wənāgōllū kassēper haššāmāyim wəkol-ṣəbāʾām yibbōl kinbōl ʿāleh miggepen ūkənōbelet mittəʾēnāh

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־רִוְּתָ֥ה בַשָּׁמַ֖יִם חַרְבִּ֑י הִנֵּה֙ עַל־אֱד֣וֹם תֵּרֵ֔ד וְעַל־עַ֥ם חֶרְמִ֖י לְמִשְׁפָּֽט׃

i18n.en: For my sword has drunk its fill in the skies; behold, it shall come down upon Edom, and upon the people I have devoted to destruction, for judgment.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־רִוְּתָ֥ה בַשָּׁמַ֖יִם חַרְבִּ֑י הִנֵּה֙ עַל־אֱד֣וֹם תֵּרֵ֔ד וְעַל־עַ֥ם חֶרְמִ֖י לְמִשְׁפָּֽט׃

notes.official:
*Kî-riwwᵉṯāh ḇaš-šāmayim ḥarbî*, “For my sword has drunk its fill in the skies.” *Riwwᵉṯāh* (Piel of *rwh*, “drink one’s fill, be saturated”) pictures the sword sated in the sky, where the host of v. 4 has been struck, before it comes down on Edom; v. 7 uses the same verb for the land “drunk with blood.” *Baš-šāmayim* is “in the skies” under the central `shamayim` register rule, with NJPS “in the sky”; ASV and JPS 1917 have “in heaven” (checked 2026-11-26). The verse names the place where the sword does its work, not YHWH’s dwelling, so the divine-realm register (“the heavens”) of 14:12–13 is not used. NJPS reports that 1QIsaᵃ reads “be seen” (cf. Targum) for “be drunk.” This is taken from the NJPS note and was not checked against the scroll; MT is translated (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

*ʿAm ḥermî*, literally “the people of my ban,” is “the people I have devoted to destruction.” The noun *ḥērem* with the first-person suffix marks Edom as the object of the ban. The line renders it verbally, as NJPS does (“the people I have doomed”), so that “devote” stays visible as central `cherem-devote-to-destruction-cross-corpus` requires and the verb of v. 2 is heard again. JPS 1917 has “the people of My ban.” ASV’s “the people of my curse” merges the ban with the curse vocabulary (*ʾālāh*, *qᵉlālāh*), which the central entry keeps apart.

paragraphs.translit: kī-riwwətāh baššāmayim ḥarbī hinnēh ʿal-ʾĕdōm tērēd wəʿal-ʿam ḥermī ləmišpāṭ

paragraphs.text: חֶ֣רֶב לַיהוָ֞ה מָלְאָ֥ה דָם֙ הֻדַּ֣שְׁנָה מֵחֵ֔לֶב מִדַּ֤ם כָּרִים֙ וְעַתּוּדִ֔ים מֵחֵ֖לֶב כִּלְי֣וֹת אֵילִ֑ים כִּ֣י זֶ֤בַח לַֽיהוָה֙ בְּבָצְרָ֔ה וְטֶ֥בַח גָּד֖וֹל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אֱדֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: The sword of YHWH is filled with blood, it is made fat with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams; for YHWH has a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
i18n.he: חֶ֣רֶב לַיהוָ֞ה מָלְאָ֥ה דָם֙ הֻדַּ֣שְׁנָה מֵחֵ֔לֶב מִדַּ֤ם כָּרִים֙ וְעַתּוּדִ֔ים מֵחֵ֖לֶב כִּלְי֣וֹת אֵילִ֑ים כִּ֣י זֶ֤בַח לַֽיהוָה֙ בְּבָצְרָ֔ה וְטֶ֥בַח גָּד֖וֹל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אֱדֽוֹם׃

notes.official: *Ḥereḇ laYHWH mālᵉʾāh dām*: ASV and JPS 1917 have “The sword of YHWH [the LORD] is filled with blood.” NJPS reads *lᵉ-* as possessive in a nominal clause, “The LORD has a sword; it is sated with blood” (checked 2026-11-26). The line keeps ASV (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-34`). The verse goes on to call the slaughter a *zeḇaḥ*, “a sacrifice” (central `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`), and lists sacrificial animals and the kidney fat that belongs on the altar (Lev 3:4, 10, 15). *Ḥēleḇ* is “fat” every time it occurs in vv. 6–7 (“made fat with fat”), in place of ASV’s alternation of “fatness” and “fat.” Bozrah is a chief city of Edom (Gen 36:33; Amos 1:12), and *ʾereṣ ʾĕḏôm* is territorial, “the land of Edom” (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.translit: ḥereb laYHWH māləʾāh dām huddašnāh mēḥēleb middam kārīm wəʿattūdīm mēḥēleb kilyōt ʾēlīm kī zebaḥ laYHWH bəbāṣərāh wəṭebaḥ gādōl bəʾereṣ ʾĕdōm

paragraphs.text: וְיָרְד֤וּ רְאֵמִים֙ עִמָּ֔ם וּפָרִ֖ים עִם־אַבִּירִ֑ים וְרִוְּתָ֤ה אַרְצָם֙ מִדָּ֔ם וַעֲפָרָ֖ם מֵחֵ֥לֶב יְדֻשָּֽׁן׃

i18n.en: And the wild oxen shall come down with them, and the bullocks with the bulls; and their land shall be drunk with blood, and their dust made fat with fat.
i18n.he: וְיָרְד֤וּ רְאֵמִים֙ עִמָּ֔ם וּפָרִ֖ים עִם־אַבִּירִ֑ים וְרִוְּתָ֤ה אַרְצָם֙ מִדָּ֔ם וַעֲפָרָ֖ם מֵחֵ֥לֶב יְדֻשָּֽׁן׃

notes.official: *Rᵉʾēmîm* are “wild oxen” (ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS). *Wᵉyārᵉḏû … ʿimmām*, “shall come down with them” (ASV, JPS 1917), means that they go down in the slaughter with the sacrificial animals of v. 6. NJPS has “shall fall with them” and notes that an emendation yields “with fatted calves” (checked 2026-11-26); MT is translated (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *Pārîm ʿim-ʾabbîrîm* is “the bullocks with the bulls” (ASV); *ʾabbîrîm* is literally “mighty ones” (NJPS “mighty steers”). *Wᵉriwwᵉṯāh ʾarṣām middām* repeats the verb of v. 5: the land is “drunk with blood” as the sword was. *ʾArṣām* is territorial “their land” (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.translit: wəyārədū rəʾēmīm ʿimmām ūpārīm ʿim-ʾabbīrīm wəriwwətāh ʾarṣām middām waʿăpārām mēḥēleb yəduššān

paragraphs.text: כִּ֛י י֥וֹם נָקָ֖ם לַֽיהוָ֑ה שְׁנַ֥ת שִׁלּוּמִ֖ים לְרִ֥יב צִיּֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: For YHWH has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.
i18n.he: כִּ֛י י֥וֹם נָקָ֖ם לַֽיהוָ֑ה שְׁנַ֥ת שִׁלּוּמִ֖ים לְרִ֥יב צִיּֽוֹן׃

notes.official: *Yôm nāqām … šᵉnaṯ šillûmîm lᵉrîḇ ṣiyyôn*, “a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion” (ASV). *Rîḇ* is a legal case; JPS 1917 has “for the controversy of Zion,” NJPS “for Zion’s cause” (checked 2026-11-26).

paragraphs.translit: kī yōm nāqām laYHWH šənat šillūmīm lərīb ṣiyyōn

paragraphs.text: וְנֶהֶפְכ֤וּ נְחָלֶ֙יהָ֙ לְזֶ֔פֶת וַעֲפָרָ֖הּ לְגָפְרִ֑ית וְהָיְתָ֣ה אַרְצָ֔הּ לְזֶ֖פֶת בֹּעֵרָֽה׃

i18n.en: And its streams shall be turned into pitch, and its dust into sulfur, and its land shall become burning pitch.
i18n.he: וְנֶהֶפְכ֤וּ נְחָלֶ֙יהָ֙ לְזֶ֔פֶת וַעֲפָרָ֖הּ לְגָפְרִ֑ית וְהָיְתָ֣ה אַרְצָ֔הּ לְזֶ֖פֶת בֹּעֵרָֽה׃

notes.official: *Gop̄rîṯ* is “sulfur” under central `gophrit-va-esh-destruction-formula`, whose rationale already names this verse: Edom’s end is drawn in the colours of Sodom (Gen 19:24; Deut 29:22). ASV and JPS 1917 have “brimstone,” NJPS “sulfur” (checked 2026-11-26). *Zep̄eṯ* is “pitch.” “Its streams” are Edom’s (NJPS note “I.e., Edom’s”; ASV supplies “[Edom]”), and *ʾarṣāh* is territorial “its land” (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.translit: wənehepkū nəḥālēhā ləzepet waʿăpārāh ləgāpərīt wəhāyətāh ʾarṣāh ləzepet bōʿērāh

paragraphs.text: לַ֤יְלָה וְיוֹמָם֙ לֹ֣א תִכְבֶּ֔ה לְעוֹלָ֖ם יַעֲלֶ֣ה עֲשָׁנָ֑הּ מִדּ֤וֹר לָדוֹר֙ תֶּחֱרָ֔ב לְנֵ֣צַח נְצָחִ֔ים אֵ֥ין עֹבֵ֖ר בָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: Night and day it shall not be quenched; its smoke shall go up forever; from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it forever and ever.
i18n.he: לַ֤יְלָה וְיוֹמָם֙ לֹ֣א תִכְבֶּ֔ה לְעוֹלָ֖ם יַעֲלֶ֣ה עֲשָׁנָ֑הּ מִדּ֤וֹר לָדוֹר֙ תֶּחֱרָ֔ב לְנֵ֣צַח נְצָחִ֔ים אֵ֥ין עֹבֵ֖ר בָּֽהּ׃

paragraphs.translit: laylāh wəyōmām lōʾ tikbeh ləʿōlām yaʿăleh ʿăšānāh middōr lādōr teḥĕrāb lənēṣaḥ nəṣāḥīm ʾēn ʿōbēr bāh

paragraphs.text: וִירֵשׁ֙וּהָ֙ קָאַ֣ת וְקִפּ֔וֹד וְיַנְשׁ֥וֹף וְעֹרֵ֖ב יִשְׁכְּנוּ־בָ֑הּ וְנָטָ֥ה עָלֶ֛יהָ קַֽו־תֹ֖הוּ וְאַבְנֵי־בֹֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: But the pelican and the porcupine shall possess it, and the owl and the raven shall dwell in it; and he shall stretch over it the line of wasteland and the plummet of emptiness.
i18n.he: וִירֵשׁ֙וּהָ֙ קָאַ֣ת וְקִפּ֔וֹד וְיַנְשׁ֥וֹף וְעֹרֵ֖ב יִשְׁכְּנוּ־בָ֑הּ וְנָטָ֥ה עָלֶ֛יהָ קַֽו־תֹ֖הוּ וְאַבְנֵי־בֹֽהוּ׃

notes.official:
The creatures that take over the ruin are birds of uncertain identity, and the line keeps the ASV names where the book has no earlier decision (overlay `ruin-fauna-isaiah`). *Qāʾaṯ* is “pelican” (ASV, JPS 1917), an unclean bird at Lev 11:18 and Deut 14:17; NJPS has “jackdaws” and notes “Meaning of Heb. uncertain.” *Qippōḏ* is “porcupine” (ASV), as at 14:23, where the book already prints “the porcupine”; JPS 1917 has “bittern” and NJPS “owls.” The list of birds favours a bird, but the identification is uncertain, and the line keeps the concordance with 14:23. *Yanšôp̄* is “owl” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “great owls”), and *ʿōrēḇ* is “raven” (central `yonah-orev`, whose rationale cites this verse) (all checked 2026-11-26).

*Wᵉnāṭāh ʿāleyhā qaw-tōhû wᵉʾaḇnê-ḇōhû* splits the pair *tōhû wā-ḇōhû* of Gen 1:2, which occurs together elsewhere only at Jer 4:23. The surveyor’s line (*qaw*, overlay `qav-qav-line-isaiah`) and the plumb-stones (*ʾaḇnê*, literally “stones”) are the builder’s instruments, here stretched out to take a city apart, as at 2 Kgs 21:13 and Lam 2:8. NJPS explains: “He shall plan chaos and emptiness for it; cf. 28.17; Lam. 2.8.” The line has “the line of wasteland and the plummet of emptiness,” so that the corpus rendering of Gen 1:2 (“wasteland and emptiness,” central `tohu-vavohu`) can be recognised in English. ASV and JPS 1917 have “the line of confusion, and the plummet of emptiness,” NJPS “a line of chaos … weights of emptiness” (checked 2026-11-26). The book keeps “chaos” for *qiryaṯ-tōhû* at 24:10, and *tōhû* is “a wasteland” at 45:18, where it again names the uninhabitable land of Gen 1:2 (overlay `tohu-bare-emptiness-wasteland-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: wīrēšūhā qāʾat wəqippōd wəyanšōp wəʿōrēb yiškənū-bāh wənāṭāh ʿālēhā qaw-tōhū wəʾabnē-bōhū

paragraphs.text: חֹרֶ֥יהָ וְאֵֽין־שָׁ֖ם מְלוּכָ֣ה יִקְרָ֑אוּ וְכָל־שָׂרֶ֖יהָ יִ֥הְיוּ אָֽפֶס׃

i18n.en: Its nobles they shall call to the kingdom, but none shall be there; and all its princes shall be nothing.
i18n.he: חֹרֶ֥יהָ וְאֵֽין־שָׁ֖ם מְלוּכָ֣ה יִקְרָ֑אוּ וְכָל־שָׂרֶ֖יהָ יִ֥הְיוּ אָֽפֶס׃

notes.official: *Ḥōreyhā wᵉʾên-šām mᵉlûḵāh yiqrāʾû* is a crux. NJPS notes “Meaning of Heb. uncertain” and renders “It shall be called, ‘No kingdom is there’” (checked 2026-11-26). The line keeps ASV, “Its nobles they shall call to the kingdom, but none shall be there”: the *ḥōrîm*, the freeborn nobles (cf. 1 Kgs 21:8), would be summoned to proclaim a king, and there is no one. JPS 1917 rearranges the clause: “As for her nobles, none shall be there to be called to the kingdom.” Many commentators suppose that a word has fallen out before *ḥōreyhā*, perhaps another creature name (recalled, not verified) (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-34`).

paragraphs.translit: ḥōrēhā wəʾēn-šām məlūkāh yiqrāʾū wəkol-śārēhā yihyū ʾāpes

paragraphs.text: וְעָלְתָ֤ה אַרְמְנֹתֶ֙יהָ֙ סִירִ֔ים קִמּ֥וֹשׂ וָח֖וֹחַ בְּמִבְצָרֶ֑יהָ וְהָיְתָה֙ נְוֵ֣ה תַנִּ֔ים חָצִ֖יר לִבְנ֥וֹת יַעֲנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And thorns shall come up in its palaces, nettles and thistles in its fortresses; and it shall be a habitation of jackals, a court for ostriches.
i18n.he: וְעָלְתָ֤ה אַרְמְנֹתֶ֙יהָ֙ סִירִ֔ים קִמּ֥וֹשׂ וָח֖וֹחַ בְּמִבְצָרֶ֑יהָ וְהָיְתָה֙ נְוֵ֣ה תַנִּ֔ים חָצִ֖יר לִבְנ֥וֹת יַעֲנָֽה׃

notes.official:
The ruin becomes *nᵉwēh ṯannîm*, “a habitation of jackals.” *Tannîm* is the plural of *tan* “jackal,” as at 13:22, 35:7 and 43:20. It is a different word from *tannîn* “dragon, sea monster” (27:1; central `taninim`), and that entry is not applied. JPS 1917 has “wild-dogs,” NJPS “jackals” (overlay `ruin-fauna-isaiah`).

*Ḥāṣîr li-ḇnôṯ yaʿănāh* is “a court for ostriches” (ASV). *Ḥāṣîr* here is “enclosure, abode,” related to *ḥāṣēr* “court” (BDB, recalled), not *ḥāṣîr* “grass” (35:7; 40:6–8). JPS 1917 has “an enclosure,” NJPS “an abode” (checked 2026-11-26) (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-34`). *Bᵉnôṯ yaʿănāh* are “ostriches,” as at 13:21 and 43:20. *Sîrîm*, *qimmôś wā-ḥôaḥ* are “thorns … nettles and thistles” (ASV).

paragraphs.translit: wəʿālətāh ʾarmənōtēhā sīrīm qimmōś wāḥōaḥ bəmibṣārēhā wəhāyətāh nəwēh tannīm ḥāṣīr libnōt yaʿănāh

paragraphs.text: וּפָגְשׁ֤וּ צִיִּים֙ אֶת־אִיִּ֔ים וְשָׂעִ֖יר עַל־רֵעֵ֣הוּ יִקְרָ֑א אַךְ־שָׁם֙ הִרְגִּ֣יעָה לִּילִ֔ית וּמָצְאָ֥ה לָ֖הּ מָנֽוֹחַ׃

i18n.en: And desert creatures shall meet with hyenas, and the wild goat shall cry to its fellow; yes, there the night-monster shall settle, and shall find for herself a place of rest.
i18n.he: וּפָגְשׁ֤וּ צִיִּים֙ אֶת־אִיִּ֔ים וְשָׂעִ֖יר עַל־רֵעֵ֣הוּ יִקְרָ֑א אַךְ־שָׁם֙ הִרְגִּ֣יעָה לִּילִ֔ית וּמָצְאָ֥ה לָ֖הּ מָנֽוֹחַ׃

notes.official:
*ʾAḵ-šām hirgîʿāh lîlîṯ ûmāṣᵉʾāh lāh mānôaḥ*. *Lîlîṯ* occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible. Philologically it is the Akkadian *lilītu*, a female demon of the *lilû* class, beside the masculine *lilû* and the *ardat-lilî*, the “maiden of the *lilû*” (CAD L, s.v. *lilītu*; recalled). The class name is usually traced to Sumerian *líl* “wind, breath”; in Hebrew the word was heard as if derived from *layil* “night.” The line keeps “the night-monster” of ASV and JPS 1917. That rendering follows the Hebrew hearing of the word as a creature of the night and the public-domain baseline, not the Akkadian–Sumerian philology, but it does keep the word a class of demon rather than a personal name (overlay `lilit-night-monster-isaiah-34`). NJPS “the lilith,” a lower-case class noun, is the alternative that follows the philology; the founder kept “the night-monster” (sign-off 2026-11-26). NJPS prints “the lilith” with the note “A kind of demon” (checked 2026-11-26). KJV has “the screech owl” (checked): it takes *lîlîṯ* as a bird, although it renders *śāʿîr* in the same verse as “the satyr.” NRSV “Lilith,” RSV “the night hag,” LXX *onokentauroi* and Vulgate *lamia* are recalled and not verified. The feminine verbs *hirgîʿāh* and *māṣᵉʾāh lāh* are kept: “shall settle, and shall find for herself a place of rest.”

*Ṣiyyîm* “desert creatures” and *ʾiyyîm* “hyenas” are rendered as at 13:21–22 (overlay `ruin-fauna-isaiah`). ASV has “the wild beasts of the desert … the wolves,” JPS 1917 “the wild-cats … the jackals,” NJPS “Wildcats … hyenas” (checked 2026-11-26). NJPS notes that most of the creatures in vv. 14–15 cannot be identified with certainty.

*Wᵉśāʿîr ʿal-rēʿēhû yiqrāʾ* is “the wild goat shall cry to its fellow” (ASV), following 13:21, where *śᵉʿîrîm* is “wild goats” and the mythological reading is given in commentary (overlay `lexical-cruxes-wave-i2-isaiah`). JPS 1917 has “the satyr,” NJPS “Goat-demons shall greet each other.” The corpus prints “goat-demons” for the same noun at Lev 17:7 (leviticus-woh overlay `seirim-goat-demons-leviticus-17-7`). There the *śᵉʿîrîm* receive sacrifices, so they must be beings that can be worshipped. Isaiah’s lists of creatures in a ruin lack that condition, and the animal sense is kept, so the corpus renders the one noun two ways by context. Here the neighbouring *lîlîṯ* makes the demonic reading stronger than at 13:21. The founder kept “the wild goat” here and “wild goats” at 13:21, with “goat-demons” reported as the alternative (sign-off 2026-11-26).

The later figure of Lilith grows out of this verse and its Mesopotamian background. The Songs of the Sage from Qumran (4Q510–511) name *lylyt* among the demons, and the Babylonian Talmud knows a female demon called Lilith, with long hair (b. ʿErub. 100b) and wings (b. Nid. 24b), who seizes those who sleep alone in a house (b. Šabb. 151b). The story of Lilith as Adam’s first wife appears first in the medieval *Alphabet of Ben Sira* (B. Hutter, “Lilith,” *DDD*, 2nd ed., 1999). These references are recalled and not verified. The capitalised personal name brings that later figure into Isaiah, which is why the line keeps the class noun.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim; claim type: speculative).** None of the canon texts in data-library (*The Book Which Tells the Truth*, *Extraterrestrials Took Me to Their Planet*, *Let's Welcome the Extraterrestrials*) cites Isa 34:14 or names Lilith, so no canon reading is quoted. The project’s wiki records the tradition of Lilith as Adam’s first wife (*Adam and Eve*) and the Mesopotamian *lilītu* (*Satan*) as comparative context and does not adopt either. A reading that linked the *lîlîṯ* of this verse to the Eden narrative would rest on that medieval tradition, not on Isaiah or the canon. Nothing in the line or the glossary depends on it.

paragraphs.translit: ūpāgəšū ṣiyyīm ʾet-ʾiyyīm wəśāʿīr ʿal-rēʿēhū yiqrāʾ ʾak-šām hirgīʿāh līlīt ūmāṣəʾāh lāh mānōaḥ

paragraphs.text: שָׁ֣מָּה קִנְּנָ֤ה קִפּוֹז֙ וַתְּמַלֵּ֔ט וּבָקְעָ֖ה וְדָגְרָ֣ה בְצִלָּ֑הּ אַךְ־שָׁ֛ם נִקְבְּצ֥וּ דַיּ֖וֹת אִשָּׁ֥ה רְעוּתָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: There the dart-snake shall make her nest, and lay, and hatch, and gather under her shade; yes, there the kites shall be gathered, each one with her mate.
i18n.he: שָׁ֣מָּה קִנְּנָ֤ה קִפּוֹז֙ וַתְּמַלֵּ֔ט וּבָקְעָ֖ה וְדָגְרָ֣ה בְצִלָּ֑הּ אַךְ־שָׁ֛ם נִקְבְּצ֥וּ דַיּ֖וֹת אִשָּׁ֥ה רְעוּתָֽהּ׃

notes.official: *Qippôz*, which occurs only here, is “dart-snake” (ASV; JPS 1917 “arrowsnake”; NJPS “arrow-snake”; checked 2026-11-26). KJV’s “great owl” (checked) reflects the verbs, which suit a bird: she nests, lays, hatches and gathers under her shade. The creature cannot be identified with certainty (NJPS note at v. 14). *Dayyôṯ* are “kites” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “buzzards”); *dayyāh* is an unclean bird at Deut 14:13 (overlay `ruin-fauna-isaiah`). *ʾIššāh rᵉʿûṯāh*, literally “a woman her companion,” is the Hebrew idiom for “each … the other” with feminine nouns, rendered “each one with her mate” (ASV); it returns in v. 16.

paragraphs.translit: šāmmāh qinnənāh qippōz wattəmallēṭ ūbāqəʿāh wədāgərāh bəṣillāh ʾak-šām niqbəṣū dayyōt ʾiššāh rəʿūtāh

paragraphs.text: דִּרְשׁ֨וּ מֵֽעַל־סֵ֤פֶר יְהוָה֙ וּֽקְרָ֔אוּ אַחַ֤ת מֵהֵ֙נָּה֙ לֹ֣א נֶעְדָּ֔רָה אִשָּׁ֥ה רְעוּתָ֖הּ לֹ֣א פָקָ֑דוּ כִּֽי־פִי֙ ה֣וּא צִוָּ֔ה וְרוּח֖וֹ ה֥וּא קִבְּצָֽן׃

i18n.en: Seek out of the scroll of YHWH, and read: not one of these shall be missing; none shall lack her mate; for my mouth, it has commanded, and his spirit, it has gathered them.
i18n.he: דִּרְשׁ֨וּ מֵֽעַל־סֵ֤פֶר יְהוָה֙ וּֽקְרָ֔אוּ אַחַ֤ת מֵהֵ֙נָּה֙ לֹ֣א נֶעְדָּ֔רָה אִשָּׁ֥ה רְעוּתָ֖הּ לֹ֣א פָקָ֑דוּ כִּֽי־פִי֙ ה֣וּא צִוָּ֔ה וְרוּח֖וֹ ה֥וּא קִבְּצָֽן׃

notes.official:
*Diršû mēʿal-sēp̄er YHWH ûqᵉrāʾû*, “Seek out of the scroll of YHWH, and read.” *Sēp̄er* is “scroll,” the same word as the rolled-up sky of v. 4, under overlay `sefer-sealed-scroll-isaiah-29`: in the eighth century a *sēp̄er* is a written roll, and “book” (ASV, JPS 1917) suggests a codex. NJPS has “the scroll of the LORD” (checked 2026-11-26). The verse does not say which scroll is meant. Commentators propose a written collection of prophecy (cf. 30:8) or a register kept by YHWH in which the creatures are listed (cf. Exod 32:32–33; Ps 139:16) (recalled, not verified). The line names the object and leaves the reference open. *ʾAḥaṯ mēhēnnāh lōʾ neʿdārāh*, “not one of these shall be missing”: the creatures of vv. 11–15 are all present, as the scroll says.

*Kî-p̄î hûʾ ṣiwwāh wᵉrûḥô hûʾ qibbᵉṣān*: MT has “my mouth” beside “his spirit,” a change of person within the line. ASV and JPS 1917 keep “My mouth”; NJPS emends to “His mouth” with the note “Heb. ‘My’” (checked 2026-11-26). A 1QIsaᵃ reading “his mouth” is reported in the secondary literature but was not checked. MT is translated (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`); shifts between the prophet’s voice and YHWH’s are frequent in prophetic speech. *Rûḥô* is “his spirit,” lower case, under overlay `ruach-divine-spirit-lower-case-isaiah` (ASV “his Spirit”; NJPS “His spirit”). JPS 1917 refers the suffix to the mouth, “the breath thereof,” which suits the pairing of mouth and breath at Ps 33:6; that reading is recorded here.

paragraphs.translit: diršū mēʿal-sēper YHWH ūqərāʾū ʾaḥat mēhēnnāh lōʾ neʿdārāh ʾiššāh rəʿūtāh lōʾ pāqādū kī-pī hūʾ ṣiwwāh wərūḥō hūʾ qibbəṣān

paragraphs.text: וְהֽוּא־הִפִּ֤יל לָהֶן֙ גּוֹרָ֔ל וְיָד֛וֹ חִלְּקַ֥תָּה לָהֶ֖ם בַּקָּ֑ו עַד־עוֹלָם֙ יִֽירָשׁ֔וּהָ לְד֥וֹר וָד֖וֹר יִשְׁכְּנוּ־בָֽהּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And he has cast the lot for them, and his hand has divided it to them by line; they shall possess it forever; from generation to generation they shall dwell in it.
i18n.he: וְהֽוּא־הִפִּ֤יל לָהֶן֙ גּוֹרָ֔ל וְיָד֛וֹ חִלְּקַ֥תָּה לָהֶ֖ם בַּקָּ֑ו עַד־עוֹלָם֙ יִֽירָשׁ֔וּהָ לְד֥וֹר וָד֖וֹר יִשְׁכְּנוּ־בָֽהּ׃ (ס)

notes.official: *Hippîl lāhen gôrāl*, “he has cast the lot for them,” and *yāḏô ḥillᵉqattāh lāhem baq-qāw*, “his hand has divided it to them by line,” use the language of the allotment of the land (Num 26:55; Josh 18:6–10). The measuring line of v. 11 (*qaw*, overlay `qav-qav-line-isaiah`), stretched over the city to undo it, now portions out the ruin to the creatures as their holding. *Yîrāšûhā*, “they shall possess it,” repeats the verb of v. 11 and closes the passage on the creatures.

paragraphs.translit: wəhūʾ-hippīl lāhen gōrāl wəyādō ḥilləqattāh lāhem baqqāw ʿad-ʿōlām yīrāšūhā lədōr wādōr yiškənū-bāh (s)
